scopeCompact offline presentation of retained native outputs. PNGs are byte copies; no rendering or image enhancement is performed here. Float film SHA-256 values come from native result records; large films are not copied or rehashed by this builder. A flagged intensity outlier may be localized by read-only access to its original float film. Matched benchmark fields are checked. A nonblack finite film is output evidence, not an unbiasedness or convergence proof. Preview filtering, finite angular resolution and omitted camera-side specular sheet paths introduce bias. First-pass, steady-pass and process-launch timings are distinct measurements.
array fields aboveCounts of retained inputs, benchmark families, capture groups, jobs and charts. Detailed per-run records follow below.

formulae
mu_mmean over K independently keyed N-pass linear RGB films for method m
mu_poolequal-weight mean of mu_m over every required method in this condition
Dsum over all pixels and RGB channels of mu_pool squared
V_msum over all pixels and channels of sample variance (ddof=1) across K films, divided by D
perPassProxyN * V_m
costmedian across K runs of 1000 * renderPassSeconds / measuredPasses
varianceCostProxyN * V_m * cost
estimatedTotalRenderingMsN * post-warmup median milliseconds/pass (warmup film samples are not free)
meanEnergymean over pixels of Rec.709 RGB luminance, then mean over seed runs
energyRatiomethod meanEnergy / equal-weight pooled method meanEnergy
scopeEmpirical seed-to-seed dispersion of this implementation. There is no ground-truth image in this analysis; these are not MSE measurements., The common normalization includes each tested method and is itself estimated. It permits within-condition comparison and cannot prove correct energy., Whole-frame RGB variance includes every pixel; no brightness-dependent mask or clipping is used in numerical analysis., N*variance assumes a per-pass scale only as a descriptive proxy. A finite run does not prove finite variance, asymptotic convergence or absence of bias., A small number of seed-key runs can miss rare singular events. Values and rankings are exploratory; no confidence intervals are claimed., The same key set is used across methods. Cross-method paired streams can be correlated; no independence assumption between methods is needed for each method variance., One pass draws one record per selected member (some members can have paired roots). A six-member pass is more work than a singleton pass., Native cost times the primary CPU renderPass only, after eight warmup passes; it excludes process initialization, UI, display, dumping and secondary films., Reported timing min/max is observed run spread, not a confidence interval. The GPU renderer string describes the display context, not a GPU implementation of the estimator., Each isolated source is centered at a common position. Full rooms also change position, overlap and source-selection probabilities; composite results cannot isolate those causes., All tested masks here are exact-sheet/directional combinations; this suite does not establish finite-radius curve bias or cross-group MIS behavior., Beauty images share one exposure and display transfer; numerical data precedes that transformation.

interpretation
observedOne finite isolated pixel dominates the high-resolution film mean. Its chromatic ratio closely matches the medium laser-like source, and its center ray crosses that source quad. This localizes the spike over the source footprint but does not identify the sampled path or primitive member.
candidateNumericalMechanismInherited sphere branch forms b*b-c and roots in float32, uses omega=(x-p)/sampled_radius, and passes it to cos^500 emission without a unit-length check or an upper cosine clamp. For a small sphere near a distant camera, cancellation/root-position error can break the sampled-radius versus recovered-distance agreement. MIS cross-evaluation recovers a normalized direction independently. This mismatch can amplify the narrow profile; it is a hypothesis, not an attribution of this exact pixel.
sourceLocationssrc/render/PPIntegrator.cpp:1611 ppEmitterDirWeight assumes normalized light direction; exponent500 has no upper cosine clamp, src/render/PPIntegrator.cpp:2499 ppSampleDirPrim sphere float discriminant/root and sampled-radius direction, src/render/PPIntegrator.cpp:2352 ppDirPrimPdf recomputes actual length/direction, src/render/PPIntegrator.cpp:6364 custom31 uses standalone contribution times MIS weight
notEstablishedWhich primitive member or pass generated the spike, Whether the root cause is a rare valid tail, arithmetic inconsistency, or another implementation issue, Infinite variance, an asymptotic tail exponent, or universal failure at high resolution, A statistical error bound for the 504 lower-resolution measurements
nextDiagnosticInstrument the exact pixel/pass and capture source label, member, sampled radius, recovered distance, direction norm, emission weight and all MIS densities; compare an independently evaluated common integrand. No such rerun performed in this batch.
